program: Free healthcare, homelessness support and care coordination
priceScope: Conditional whole annual accounting cost against selected health and signed medical/housing resource channels; not portfolio EV or marginal gift.

what: Will-Grundy Medical Clinic provides free healthcare, homelessness support and care coordination locally.
Its housing programs include tenant-based rental assistance and medical respite.
The annual illustration assesses bounded clinical health plus signed medical and housing household resources.
strengths: Original sources retain housing and clinic cost scope.
Current annual report distinguishes housing families from clinical visits.
Recognized and unrecognized resources remain separately disclosed.
reservations: Annual clinical person count is an assumed share of all-program reach.
Net cash, utility and cohort overlap remain hypotheses.
Cross-year cost matching, financial controls and marginal gift capacity remain uncertain.

sections.what: WGMC combines healthcare with homelessness support and care coordination across Will, Grundy and Kendall counties. Ordinary recipient costs include housing, administration and fundraising as well as clinic care.
sections.monitoring: The FY2025 report counts over 1,000 individuals served and 1,707 patient visits. N=1,000 is a rounded floor of all individuals, not unique medical patients; k=.5 is an assumed clinical share. Disease-control trends are uncontrolled and are not causal QALY calibration. Activity in FY2025 is paired with FY2024 audited costs, an explicit cross-year limitation. Fresh FY2025 report identifies 23 tenant-based rental-assistance families and five medical-respite participants. These are not added to clinical people or inferred to be unique incremental placements. It reports 2,100+ volunteer hours, not the older FY2024 10,000-hour figure; no current measured opportunity-cost coefficient.
sections.qualitative: Healthcare and housing can jointly protect existing households' consumption. Central medical and housing cash hypotheses are $100 each after alternative clinics/shelters, rent payment, benefits withdrawn and other costs—not retail care or gross rental grants. Earnings are zero centrally as an explicit uncertainty judgment, with signed work cases. Twenty-three observed housing families anchor a judged .5 additionality pathway; housing clinical utility remains unmeasured rather than proven zero. Nutrition/basic-needs and other care welfare also remain unknown.
sections.cost: Full FY2024 audited expense is $1,857,494, including the housing program and all support costs. It already includes $182,874 recognized in-kind equipment, supplies and prescriptions. Over 10,000 volunteer hours are unrecognized in those accounts. A separate resource sensitivity values 10,000 hours at judged $50/hour and adds $500,000; this is neither a measured opportunity cost nor a complete partner-resource estimate. Annual work removes the separate .4 gift-financing multiplier, without proving gift expansion. Clinical 500 is a judged .5 share of the 1,000-person all-program floor, unchanged by resource household grouping. Full .05 aggregate process harm survives failure. The current conditional health is3.626 and signed resources−.08410, price approximately$5.24M per ten combined equivalents; selected effects against full annual cost are not complete portfolio EV. Current volunteer-floor sensitivity2100*$50 and historical10000*$50 are separate hypotheses, not both added.
sections.funding: Audit revenue is $2,488,509, including $2,090,709 grants/contracts; net assets are $1,953,389. Finding 2024-001 reports multiple auditor adjustments needed, repeating the prior year; the audit still gives an unmodified financial opinion. Supporting documentation for all contributed services was unavailable. Prior-year net assets were restated, so tax-return values should not be treated as comparable audit totals. No priced unfunded expansion was established. Root freshly checked original Schedule D audited expense$1,857,494; return expense$1,852,483 differs. Direct full-audit retrieval failed this pass, so recognized donation/control details retain prior original acceptance rather than freshly claimed audit inspection. Resource400medicalhouseholds and23housingfamilies are maximallynested centrally by judgment, not observed union; changed subgroups jointly log cash/work minus full$25net incremental access/timecost. Positive .5overlap only reduces gains; negative costs persist when benefits fail. Baseline$20,000 is judged consumption, not the220%FPL eligibility limit. Distinct outside payer/provider stresses exclude resources already recognized in C and do not treat public grants as costless income. No priced current gift capacity. Medical financial-protection additionality is independently judged .3, not tied to clinical response; clinical null need not erase otherwise-paid cash. A zero medical resource-grouping scenario does not imply housing families disappear.

model.formula: Health=g*(N*k*a*u*T+positive-only housing health overlap-full harm)/(1+r)^delay. Resources=.5*sum(people*discounted finite years*log(after/before)*geography), joint medical/housing household flows and full costs; price10=10*C/(health+signed resources).
model.counterfactual: Medical and housing alternatives have separate judged additionality; annual work has no marginal finance factor. Free services do not prove otherwise-paid cash savings.
model.attribution: Clinical assumed patient share separate from household grouping; housing count is native families, not multiplied by household factor again. No measured utility, cash or net earnings. Other channels remain unknown, not zero.
model.uncertainty: All utility, causal response, duration, funding additionality and residence parameters are illustrative judgments, not measured causal effects, calibrated expected values, confidence intervals or marginal gift purchase prices. Different accounting treatment of donated care prevents comparative economic-efficiency rankings.
